claims.text: Issue #1241 concerns invalid first input position (0) for a match during first usage of the decompression context; the fix starts the reference at 1 instead of 0, relating to dictEnd/previousDstEnd initialization in the decompressor (dictEnd = previousDstEnd, dictEnd = NULL on reset).
window->base = ip - distanceFromBase in zstd_compress_internal.h: window base is computed relative to the current input pointer; a 0 position would yield a pointer before the buffer start.

Indexing scheme: 'All regular indexes relative to this position' (base) and dictBase for extDict; positions are pointers-offsets, so position 0 is undefined/invalid when the context is first used and base is not yet established.
ZSTD_insertBt1() adds positions to the match-finding tree; a 0 start would place an invalid (base-relative zero) entry in the tree before any input is consumed.
Window maintenance drops first positions when the window grows too large, matching the sliding-window pointer arithmetic that requires every stored position to be a valid buffer offset.

Context is first used during dictionary loading in ZSTD_loadDictionaryContent (lib/compress/zstd_compress.c, ~lines 2615-2694), invoked at line 2803 when preparing the CCtx; this is where match state input positions for the context get initialized before compression begins.

The initial input position for matches is governed by dictStartIndex in the match finders: in lib/compress/zstd_fast.c (line 66) and lib/compress/zstd_double_fast.c (line 77), dictStartIndex is set when dictMode == ZSTD_dictMatchState, establishing the first valid input position for a match.

Match validity is checked against dictStartIndex boundaries (e.g., zstd_fast.c lines 132/276/308, zstd_double_fast.c lines 389/400/407/446); per issue #1241, the fix starts the reference at 1 instead of 0 so the first input position is valid even on first context usage.
